definition: The Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) is a neural processing unit (NPU) application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed by Google for neural network machine learning.
details: Tensorflow, Jax, and PyTorch are supported frameworks for TPU. Google began using TPUs internally in 2015, and in 2018 made them available for third-party use, both as part of its cloud infrastructure and by offering a smaller version of the chip for sale. Currently, Google Cloud generates product revenues primarily from the sale of TPU systems.

explainer.lead: The Tensor Processing Unit is a Google-developed neural processing unit, an application-specific integrated circuit built for neural network machine learning. It matters because it trades general-purpose flexibility for high-volume, low-precision computation efficiency, and underpins Google Cloud's product revenues.

tiers.eli5: It is a chip built only for the kind of maths neural networks do, like a calculator specialised for one job instead of a full computer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run TensorFlow, JAX and PyTorch workloads on TPUs, which suit convolutional networks especially well. The pitfall is precision: TPUs target as little as 8-bit computation, so accuracy-sensitive work may need different hardware.
tiers.paperLevel: An NPU ASIC for neural network machine learning, designed for high-volume low-precision computation with more input/output operations per joule and no rasterisation or texture-mapping hardware. TPUs suit CNNs; GPUs have benefits for some fully connected networks, CPUs for some recurrent networks.

explainer.example: A team trains a convolutional image classifier on TensorFlow using TPUs in Google Cloud, accepting 8-bit precision to gain throughput per joule.
